notes: Written from the guide's 'Game plan by turn' and 'Playbook seeds'.

goFirst false: the guide says 'going second is the big swing for this deck: two ramps reach 10 DON!! on T4' [SH-ROB]; Shonen's simulation has Linlin castable by T4 in 55% of games going second against 22% going first.

cardValue: ongoing effects named in the guide's Defining cards (Linlin's 8000 base power for every 4000-base Trigger Character, Yamato's Blocker and ramp, Sweet 3 Generals' Life refill). The sizes are inferences.
weights.don 1.3: the deck is a ramp deck whose leader adds a rested DON!! per attack [SH-ROB]; inference: next turn's DON!! counts for more here than in the default heuristic.

counterAggression 0.9: 'roughly 29 of the 50 cards carry a [Trigger], so taking hits also develops the board' [SH-ROB]; inference: a hit costs this deck a little less than the default, so it counters slightly less readily.

faceBias 1.0/1.0/1.1: the guide's plan builds for turns and attacks with the 8000-power bodies from the Linlin turn onward [SH-ROB]; inference: slightly more weight on the opponent's Life late. Every number here is an inference (review M5a-09).

Seed 5 (two 8000-power Trigger attackers on the Linlin turn) is the guide's own inference. The planted position showed search alone leaves the 8000-power bodies home, so it has an attackWithPower bias: a Character with a [Trigger] and 8000 power or more (derived, so only while Linlin is on the field) attacks.
The Pudding bias has two parts: the play (turn 3 at the latest) and paying her cost (trash a Trigger card to draw 3).
The pitch bias carries donDeckAtLeast 1: with the DON!! deck empty the pitch is legal but adds nothing (RL-50), so it is not rewarded.
Citations ('cite', 'citeSource') are what 'Why?' shows when a move follows the line; every condition here is public (a play, an attack, a trashed card).

Bias sizes were raised from 1.0 after the first Pirate-vs-Pirate run: 2.0 for the Leader attack and 2.5 for the pitch (at 1.0 the pitch was declined in 17% of attacks and the Leader stayed home in 12% of qualifying turns), and 3.0 for Yamato (at 2.0 the AI played Pudding on T2 instead, in 4 of 6 misses; the guide plays Yamato on T2 and Pudding on T3).
